title: Robot — Indian automata
text:
Title: Robot — Indian automata

11th century texts of Buddhist mythology also describe automata. Examples include the Samarangana Sutradhara, a treatise by Bhoja (king of Malwa) which includes a chapter about the construction of mechanical automata, including mechanical bees and birds, fountains shaped like humans and animals, and male and female dolls that refilled oil lamps, danced, played instruments, and re-enacted scenes from Hindu mythology. The Lokapannatti is an 11th-12th century Buddhist cosmological text that tells of how the Buddha's relics were protected by mechanical robots (bhuta vahana yanta or "spirit movement machines") until they were disarmed by King Ashoka.
